title: Cross-engine floating-point determinism is unverified: Math.hypot/sin/cos in the per-step path can differ between V8 and JavaScriptCore
note: Premise confirmed, consequence not. Mechanism is as described: physics.ts:16 len() uses Math.hypot in the per-step collision path and circleRectOverlap (:275); engine.ts:217 uses Math.cos/sin at shot time; Math.pow(damp, dt*60) is safe since (1/60)*60===1. I verified empirically (Node v20.20.0, exact-integer inputs where sqrt(x*x+y*y) is provably correctly rounded) that V8's Math.hypot disagrees with the correctly-rounded result on ~35% of samples (710,632/2,000,000), so engines using libm hypot (JSC/SpiderMonkey) will differ in the last bit, and collision code branches on distance comparisons. However, no v1 flow ever runs the same inputs on two engines: server/rooms.ts is the sole simulator online (clients in src/net/GameClient.ts only deserialize+render, no prediction/lockstep/rollback); solo play simulates in one browser; the existing URL share (?state= read at GameCanvas.tsx:18; buildStateUrl has no caller) is a full-state snapshot that the receiver simulates forward alone, which is cross-browser safe regardless of ulp drift, so the claim's assertion that the URL-share feature is not cross-browser safe is wrong for what is implemented. There is no input log or replay feature anywhere (grep for inputLog/shotHistory/replay in src+server is empty); input-log replays, async, lockstep are Phase 5 / "later if needed" per CLAUDE.md. CLAUDE.md §7 asks for "same inputs -> same outputs, bit-identical" tests, which the same-engine test satisfies. Not a polish or release gap for v1. Cheap future-proofing (hypot -> Math.sqrt(x*x+y*y), since IEEE sqrt is correctly rounded on all engines) is reasonable to do opportunistically; a cross-engine golden-hash test is scope creep until a replay/lockstep feature exists.

title: A ball cannot rest on a hazard ward and bounces with growing amplitude until it drifts off
note: Mechanism is accurately described (physics.ts:216 bounce 1.05 for hazards, :224-225 hazards never set grounded, so the :136 rest check can't pass while touching a ward), but the claimed symptom does not occur under realistic play. I re-simulated on Hazard Cavern (level 2, blue ward at x=560, w=22, h=100, wind 14) with a red ball via stepBall. With any shot-plausible landing velocity (min shot speed is 88 px/s; tested vx 88-250, vy 300-500) the ball touches the ward top for exactly ONE contact frame and leaves the 22 px top within 0.10-0.28 s; the remaining 2-4 s is ordinary downstream terrain settling after an energetic rebound, which is indistinguishable from hitting the ward's side (the intended 'hazard repels you' behavior). The multi-contact 'growing amplitude' case only appears with a contrived dead-center drop at vx=0 (2-3 contacts, leaves at ~1.5 s, apex growth ~3 px: 30 -> 33 px), which a shot cannot produce because the ball starts on terrain, every shot has horizontal speed, and the level's wind guarantees drift. Even then the extra contacts cost ~1 s and a couple of 5-particle sparks, visually reading as the hazard rejecting the ball. A hostile ward being un-restable is arguably desirable (a safe perch on top of a 'hazard' would be a worse reading). Not a polish gap worth fixing for v1; at most a note that hazard restitution > 1 is a design choice. Scratch scripts: C:\Users\KevnP\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-KevnP\9008f5d3-9b42-45ce-82f6-49cf5037798e\scratchpad\ward_rest.ts and ward_rest2.ts.

title: players/golfers/balls are parallel arrays indexed by activePlayerIndex with strokes, colours and RNG types duplicated
note: Mechanism is accurately described (parallel arrays indexed by activePlayerIndex; strokes mirrored at engine.ts:219-220; palette/Rng type duplicated), but the claimed bad behaviour cannot occur in v1: shoot() is the sole stroke mutator and resetLevel/nextLevel rebuild all arrays together, playerCount is fixed at creation, nothing reorders the arrays, deserializeState round-trips the whole object, and online player ids are fixed 0=host/1=guest with server/rooms.ts handleDisconnect destroying the room (no reconnect, leave, or drop-in path exists). The desync triggers cited (drop-in/leave, reconnect, 3-4 players) are explicit Phase 5+ non-goals in CLAUDE.md section 4, so preparing for them is scope expansion the project rules say to decline. Hazard palette mismatch (blue and gold differ by 1-2 hex digits) only tints the 5-particle hazard splash and is imperceptible. Not a polish gap for a v1 release; at most an optional 10-minute hygiene tidy (export RngState once, reuse playerColors in render.ts:390, share hazard hex values).

title: Guest never receives peerJoined, so the lobby says 'Waiting for host...' while the host is present
note: Mechanism is accurately described: rooms.ts:115 sends peerJoined only to the host, GameClient.ts:92-96 leaves the guest at peerConnected:false, so Lobby.tsx:127's 'Host will start the game.' branch and the joined-side of the peerJoined handler are unreachable, and roomCreated+waiting (rooms.ts:132-133) are redundant. But there is no user-visible defect: a guest can only be in 'joined' while the host socket is alive (joinRoom needs an existing room; handleDisconnect destroys the room and errors the guest if the host drops), so 'Waiting for host…' is shown exactly when the guest is waiting on the host to press Start, which is what the text means to a player. The Start transition is the same screen change the host sees. This is a dead-code / redundant-message hygiene nit (optionally reword to 'Waiting for host to start…' and drop the dead branch), not a polish gap that matters for v1.

title: Colour 'hazard' wards read as danger walls, not per-player doors; naming and HUD give no explanation
note:
Mechanism partly as described, but the claim's premise and key assertions are wrong.

What is accurate: render.ts:93-97 draws a hazard rect as a filled, glow-blurred pillar in red/blue/green/gold; physics.ts:206 skips collision entirely when rect.color === ball.safeColor; non-matching balls bounce at 1.05 (physics.ts:216) with a particle burst (:223); a matching pass-through has no particle/visual feedback; the level hint (levels.ts:157) says "Matching players pass wards." and the scoreboard (render.ts:332) prints "P1 red".

What is refuted:
1. "Per-player doors" / "P1 can never pass the blue ward in 1-player": false. The wards are 22px-wide, 88/100px-tall pillars on a 800px-tall level; artillery shots arc over them. Scratch sim (createGameState(1, 2) + stepBall, red ball from the start) lands past the blue ward (x>582) at power 80 for every angle 40-60 deg and at power 100 for all angles tested (rest x up to 1749). Mismatched wards are bouncy speed bumps that can kick a low shot back toward the tee (power 70 -> rest x=12), not blockers. The hint's "spring and fan help reach the upper lane" is also consistent with the level being completable solo.
2. "Only hint is the word 'red' on the scoreboard": incomplete. Each ward carries its own label ("RED"/"BLUE", render.ts:125), the ward hue is the player's own ball colour (#ff4f6d vs ball #ff5d73; #46b7ff vs #50b7ff), and the hint line is on screen for the whole level. Red = "mine" for the red player is an internally consistent mapping, and the claimed "red = danger" conflict is weakened because contact is non-lethal (no reset, no stroke penalty, just a bounce).
3. "The code calls it hazard" is a code-only naming point invisible to players; irrelevant for release polish.

What survives is small: (a) a matching ball passing through gets no feedback while a mismatched ball gets particles, and (b) whether players read the glow as "danger" is exactly the kind of readability question CLAUDE.md §8.4 says to answer with playtesters, not reasoning. That is a low-priority polish note for the Phase 3 art pass ("readable hazards"), not a confirmed design flaw. Suggested fix (striped force-field + ball glyph + "P1 can pass" tag) is scope beyond what the evidence justifies.

title: HUD and all menus are drawn on canvas with literal pixel coordinates, contradicting CLAUDE.md s7 (React for menu/HUD overlays) and making layout, hit-testing and text state fragile
note: Partially accurate description, but the core mechanism and the "contradicts CLAUDE.md" framing do not hold. Facts confirmed: drawHud/drawStart/drawLevelComplete/drawCampaignComplete (src/game/render.ts:300-554) are canvas-drawn with computed pixel coords, no wrapping or hit-testing; drawHud sets no textAlign/textBaseline; overlays reset state manually at :415-416, :435, :552-553; drawPlatforms sets lineCap outside save at :78. Refutations: (1) The "fragile text state" mechanism is wrong. renderGame wraps all world drawing in ctx.save() (:20) / ctx.restore() (:32) before drawHud runs (:34); save/restore captures textAlign, textBaseline, lineCap, font, globalAlpha, so no world draw function (including the :78 lineCap leak, which doesn't affect text anyway) can shift HUD text. Only the overlay functions themselves can leak and each resets what it touches. (2) CLAUDE.md §7 says "React for menu/HUD overlays only (PR #2 model)", which bounds React usage rather than mandating a React HUD; the PR #2 React menu exists (src/Lobby.tsx, src/App.tsx online-bar) and README.md:22 documents the intended split as "HTML5 Canvas for the game, React for the app shell". Not a contradiction. (3) "No buttons/no accessibility": the whole game is keyboard-only (src/game/input.ts binds only keydown/keyup, no pointer input at all), so a non-hit-tested canvas HUD is consistent; mobile/touch is Phase 4/5 per CLAUDE.md §5/§6. The one real wart is drawStart drawing four button-looking tiles (:398-409) that cannot be clicked, which is a small separate UX finding. (4) The concrete symptoms are minor and fixable in place: HUD panel vs scoreboard overlap only below ~738px width (where a keyboard-only game is unplayable anyway); the fixed ~45px .online-bar does cover the top of the HUD title in online mode, a one-line offset fix. Verdict: a canvas HUD is standard for a scrappy-Flash keyboard+gamepad desktop-web game and is working; rewriting four screens into React is refactor scope with no player-visible payoff, which CLAUDE.md §3/§8 (ship before scope, solo dev, default no) argues against. Not a gap that matters for the defined v1.

title: OnlineSession couples network tick rate to React render rate: the React tree re-renders 60x/s from server ticks and mixes data with callbacks
note:
Mechanism is mostly as described but the measured impact is negligible, and the forward-looking justification is out of v1 scope.

Confirmed: server broadcasts a full gameState every tick at 60Hz (server/rooms.ts:106, :73-82); GameClient.onMessage allocates a new OnlineSession per message via buildSession() (src/net/GameClient.ts:106-118, :128-138); OnlineGame does setSession(next.session) per emit (src/App.tsx:40-47), so OnlineGame, the online-bar and GameCanvas re-render at tick rate; GameCanvas uses an eager `useRef(readStateFromUrl() ?? createGameState(2))` initializer (src/game/GameCanvas.tsx:18) that re-runs every render; GameClient imports createGameState from the engine for a placeholder (GameClient.ts:1, :20).

Partly wrong: "Lobby re-fires onOnlinePlay" is only transient. Once App switches mode to 'online', Lobby unmounts and its subscribe cleanup removes the listener (Lobby.tsx:14-19), so at most 0-1 extra setMode calls happen before commit; there is no sustained double subscription.

Why it does not matter for a polished v1: measured with npx tsx against the real engine, createGameState(2) is ~13 us/call (about 0.8 ms of CPU per second at 60Hz, <0.1% of the 16.7 ms frame budget); URLSearchParams parse is ~0.4 us. The React tree re-rendered per tick is ~7 elements (three spans, a button, one <canvas>); reconciliation of that at 60Hz is tens of microseconds. GameCanvas's useEffect has [] deps so the rAF loop, input bindings and resize listener are created once; re-renders only update onlineRef. No behavioral bug results: the canvas reads the latest state via the ref each frame and the HUD's "your turn / waiting" text is derived display that legitimately needs the per-tick phase. deserializeState (~15 us/msg) is required by the chosen 60Hz state-broadcast design regardless of this structure. The engine import in GameClient adds no bundle cost (the client already bundles the engine for local play); it is a cosmetic coupling (latestState could be GameState | null). The unused `startGame` on OnlineSession is dead surface but harmless.

The "growing this object" argument cites reconnection, latency display and spectators; none are in the Phase 3 v1 scope in CLAUDE.md, and spectators/more players are explicitly on the §4 cut list. CLAUDE.md §8 says to default to no on new scope and to distinguish modularity from indecision; this refactor is a nice-to-have, not a release blocker. A one-line lazy ref init would remove the only measurable (and still trivial) waste. Severity: low.

title: Keyboard-only start screen will not respond inside itch.io/Newgrounds iframes until the player clicks the game
note: Refuted. The claim's premise (iframe has no keyboard focus until clicked) is true, but the described bad behavior cannot occur because the keyboard-only "Press 1, 2, 3, or 4" start screen is never the first thing a player sees. src/App.tsx starts in `Lobby` (DOM buttons: Create online room / Join / "Play locally (same keyboard)"); `GameCanvas` only mounts after the player clicks a lobby button inside the iframe, and that click hands the iframe keyboard focus. Verified empirically with Playwright (scratchpad/pw/iframe_focus.mjs, headless Edge, game at localhost:5199 embedded in a parent page): (A) with parent focused and no click, pressing "1" never reaches the game window (keys=[]); (B) after a real mouse click on "Play locally", game document.hasFocus()=true with activeElement=BODY (focus fixup after the button unmounts); (C) pressing "2" reaches the window keydown listener and the canvas transitions from the start panel to "Tutorial Hills" with P1/P2 scoreboard (iframe_after.png); (D) ArrowUp also reaches the game. The online path is even less affected: GameClient drops `start`-phase states and filterOnlineInput strips 1-4, so the start screen is never shown online; the host clicks Create/Start, and the `?room=` invite link is built from window.location.href (the iframe's own URL), so a guest opens it top-level, where Chrome/Firefox/Edge give the page focus on navigation commit (the "focus stays in the address bar" assertion is incorrect for mainstream browsers). itch.io's default embed additionally requires a "Run game" click. A tabIndex/focus-on-mount on the canvas would be harmless defensive polish (e.g. if a future change deep-links straight into GameCanvas without the lobby), but no gap exists in the current flow, so it is not a real polish gap for v1.

title: Switch state is written into the Level object; dynamic state lives inside static geometry
note: Mechanism is described accurately but no bad behavior follows from it, and the "flaw" runs against the project's own stated constraints. Confirmed facts: updateSwitches (physics.ts:36-40) mutates level.switches[i].pressed in place; isRectActive/isSegmentActive/liveRectPosition/dynamicRects do level.switches.find(); createGameState JSON-clones the level (engine.ts:31, :309); handleFlight calls updateSwitches twice (engine.ts:231, :233). Why it does not matter: (1) Every level has 0 or 1 switch and at most ~7 rects (levels.ts), so the linear find is nanoseconds; an O(1) rectsBySwitch index is premature. (2) The level living inside GameState with pressed embedded is exactly what CLAUDE.md §3.4/§7 require ("every game state must serialize to JSON") -- serializeState (state.ts) and the server broadcast (server/rooms.ts:63) round-trip switch state for free precisely because it is in the state; the suggested "freeze and share Level objects" would pull the level out of the serialized state and require re-resolving it by levelIndex on deserialize, which is more work for no v1 payoff. The clone is a one-time cost per level load, and grep shows levels[] is only ever accessed through cloneLevel, so there is no shared-mutation bug. (3) Press/release events for Phase 3 SFX are trivially obtainable today by reading sw.pressed before and after updateSwitches; nothing in the design blocks that. (4) Timed/weighted switches are not in the v1 scope (CLAUDE.md §4/§5: no new mechanics). (5) The duplicate updateSwitches at engine.ts:233 is a harmless, idempotent redundant line (nothing changes between the two calls) -- a one-line cleanup, not a design flaw. Net: a stylistic purity preference, not a gap that affects a polished v1. Downgraded to low.

title: vercel.json catch-all SPA rewrite is unnecessary (no path routing) and masks 404s: /ws and /favicon.ico return the HTML page with 200
note: Mechanism confirmed (catch-all rewrite, no client router, live curl shows 200 text/html for /ws, /favicon.ico, unknown paths, and /ws with Upgrade headers). But the claimed harm does not materialize. The core causal argument is wrong: the browser WebSocket API never exposes the handshake HTTP status, so a 404 vs 200 on /ws yields the identical opaque error event, and GameClient.connect() (src/net/GameClient.ts:43-49) already reduces every failure to the fixed string 'Could not connect to game server'. Removing the rewrite changes nothing user-visible. favicon.ico: index.html has no icon link and there is no public/ dir, so the browser ignores a 200-HTML response exactly as it would a 404; the missing favicon is an independent tiny polish item, not caused by the rewrite. Crawler/uptime concerns are irrelevant to a friend-shares-link game whose launch channels (itch.io/Newgrounds) host their own build copy. Deleting the rewrites block is harmless housekeeping, not a real design flaw.

title: No settings surface: no mute, no reduced motion, and colour-only hazard coding fails colourblind players
note: Mechanism partly confirmed, central bad behaviour refuted for v1 content. Confirmed: render.ts:93-97 fills hazard wards by hue only; `label()` (render.ts:580-587) draws the ward's name in dark rgba(14,20,30,.72) at rect.y-8, which for a 88-100px tall ward standing on the surface lands in the #0c0e18 sky, so the "red"/"blue" label is effectively invisible; there is no settings/mute/volume/localStorage code anywhere in src/. Refuted: (1) the only ward level, Hazard Cavern (levels.ts:169-170), defines exactly two wards, red #ff4f6d and blue #46b7ff. No green ward exists in any level, so "red and green wards are indistinguishable" describes content that does not exist; red vs blue is not a confusable pair under protan/deutan vision. The green ball (#72de72) only appears for player 3, and CLAUDE.md §4 makes >2 players a launch non-goal; even then red #ff4f6d vs green #6bed77 differ strongly in luminance (~0.33 vs ~0.68), so "indistinguishable" is overstated. The rule is also stated in text: the HUD scoreboard prints `ball.safeColor` as a word ("P1 red — N strokes", render.ts:332) and the level hint says "Matching players pass wards." (2) "Once audio exists it needs a mute toggle" is anticipatory: package.json has no audio dependency and there is no AudioContext/Audio usage, CLAUDE.md Phase 2 explicitly says "no SFX pass", so there is nothing to mute today. (3) No screen shake or strobing exists (grep for shake/flash/strobe returns nothing; only a 1.5px golfer bob, fan wave lines, and flag wobble), so a reduced-motion toggle has nothing to reduce. A settings panel with SFX/music/shake/reduced-motion/colourblind-pattern options is scope expansion against CLAUDE.md §8.1. Residual genuine items, smaller than claimed: the ward (and all rect) labels are unreadable against the sky, which touches CLAUDE.md §9 "readability of mechanics ... still required" and is a one-line fix (light label text or a backing pill); and the Phase 3 SFX task should include a mute toggle when audio is added. Neither is the claim as stated.

title: 'Gimme' is in the repo name but not in the game; a gimme rule would fit the 10-minute goal and the near-miss-heavy physics
note: Mechanism partly confirmed, premise and framing refuted. Facts: isOverHole is at src/game/terrain.ts:94-97 (not :139) with threshold hole.radius*0.85 = 13.6 px; physics.ts:6 REST_SPEED=20, :141 sinks when over hole and speed<150; engine.ts:18 MIN_POWER=10, :248 angle resets to -pi/4 each turn (power persists). No 'gimme' anywhere in src/. Refutation 1 (title): CLAUDE.md s9 explicitly decides 'Flash Gimme Golf is the repo name. The in-game title is Flash Golf', so 'gives the title a meaning players will repeat' is void; players never see the word. Refutation 2 ('often'): I ran a scratch sweep of 43,700 approach shots per level (positions 60-600 px short of the cup, full power/angle grid) through the real stepBall: balls resting within one diameter (24 px) of the cup without sinking are 0.72-1.31% of shots (7-23% as many as sinks), spread uniformly over 14-24 px on both sides, not clustered 'a few pixels past the lip'. A ball rolling over the cup on the ground at <150 px/s always sinks, so there is no lip-out; the near rests are mostly stop-shorts or bounce-overs. Cost of a near-miss is one ~4 s turn cycle, roughly one per level per pair, so the 10-minute-session impact is seconds. Refutation 3 (scope): a conceded-stroke rule is a new mechanic; CLAUDE.md Phase 2 says 'No new mechanics', s8.1 'default to saying no to new scope', s8.4 says near-miss friction is exactly a question for 5 playtesters, and the suggested fix adds a rule to teach on level 1 against the 'easy to teach' goal. If playtests do flag tap-in tedium, the in-scope tuning lever is the 0.85 hole threshold or not resetting aim between turns, not a new rule. Not a gap for v1 as CLAUDE.md defines it.
